whyTitle: Why do forms ask for a 20KB photo or signature?
whyP1: A 20KB cap keeps application servers fast and storage costs down when thousands of applicants upload photos at once — which is why it's such a common limit on Indian government recruitment portals, especially for signature uploads. SSC CGL, UPSC, IBPS bank exams, and several state PSC and railway recruitment forms specify a signature (and sometimes photo) size limit in this range, and uploads over the limit are simply rejected at submission.
whyP2: The problem is that a photo straight off a phone camera is usually 2-5MB — 100-250x too large. Resizing dimensions alone doesn't reliably hit an exact KB target, which is what this tool does directly: pick 20KB, upload your photo or signature, and download a file sized right for the form.
howP: Your photo is re-encoded to land at or under 20KB while keeping it sharp enough to pass photo-verification checks — usually no visible quality loss for a small ID-style or signature image. If you need a different size, the same tool supports custom targets like 50KB or 100KB too.
diveTitle: What to know about hitting an exact 20KB target
diveSubtitle: The details that matter for the tightest common size limit.
dive1Title: 20KB is almost always a signature limit, not a photo one
dive1Desc: Very few forms ask for a full photo at 20KB — it's tight enough to visibly degrade a face photo. Most often this exact limit appears for signature scans, which compress well because they're mostly white background with a small ink stroke.
dive2Title: How hitting an exact byte target works
dive2Desc: Rather than applying one fixed quality setting, the tool re-encodes your image at progressively lower quality until the output lands at or under 20KB — the highest quality that still fits, not a guess.
dive3Title: Why signatures compress so much further than photos
dive3Desc: A signature scan is mostly flat white space with a thin dark line, which JPEG compression handles very efficiently. A face photo has continuous tone and detail throughout the frame, so it needs far more aggressive compression to reach the same 20KB target.
dive4Title: When a photo can't fit 20KB without visible loss
dive4Desc: If quality reduction alone isn't enough to reach 20KB without noticeable artifacts, the tool also reduces the image's pixel dimensions slightly — a small resolution drop is usually less noticeable than heavy compression artifacts at full size.
dive5Title: Exam bodies that specify a 20KB signature cap
dive5Desc: SSC CGL, UPSC, IBPS bank exams, Railway RRB, and several state PSC recruitment forms commonly cap signature uploads at 20KB. Always check your specific form's instructions, since the exact number can vary even within the same exam body across years.
dive6Title: 20KB rejected even though the file size is fine?
dive6Desc: Some forms enforce both a KB cap and a minimum pixel dimension at the same time — a heavily compressed image can meet the size limit but fail a dimension check. If your upload is rejected, check the form's stated width/height requirement, not just the KB limit.
faq1Q: Which exams and forms need a 20KB photo or signature?
faq1A: Many Indian government exam and recruitment portals — SSC, UPSC, IBPS, Railway RRB, and various state PSC forms — cap the signature upload (and sometimes the photo) at 20KB. The exact limit varies by form, so double-check the instructions on your specific application before uploading.
faq2Q: Will compressing to 20KB make my photo blurry?
faq2A: Not noticeably for a small ID-photo or signature use. The tool lowers JPEG quality first and reduces pixel dimensions slightly only if it has to, so a small ID-style photo or signature stays readable.
faq3Q: What image formats can I compress to 20KB?
faq3A: JPG, PNG, and WEBP are all supported. Most exam portals ask for JPG specifically — if yours does, just upload your photo in any format and the compressed download will be sized correctly regardless.
faq4Q: Do I need to sign up or install anything?
faq4A: No. Upload your photo, get your 20KB file, done — no software to install, and the file is deleted from our servers automatically afterward.
faq5Q: Can I compress multiple photos at once?
faq5A: Yes — up to 2 images at a time on the free plan (10 on Starter, 20 on Pro). Each one is compressed to 20KB individually, and you can download them all when they're ready.
